text:
ryan_sales: @here inbound from EdgeScale — they want a dedicated pool for a new retrieval+rank chat product. Asking for guidance on sizing and whether we can guarantee <120ms p95 for 1k concurrent users (chatty), peak 3k concurrent for short bursts. They want EU tenancy, monthly commit.

mira_k: thanks Ryan. quick clarifying q: what's the expected qps per user and avg seq length?

ryan_sales: they estimate ~0.6 qps per active user (because many short messages), so steady ~600 qps at 1k concurrent, bursts to ~1800 qps. Avg input tokens ~60, output ~80. model is a 70B open model (we recommended a 7B+ or 13B variant for cost but customer wants quality).

alex_f: 70B changes everything. On A100 80GB you can maybe do ~10-15 seq/s depending on perf flags and kv cache; H100 better but more expensive. For p95 <120ms with that model and token lengths is unlikely unless you shard across many GPUs and use heavy batching optimizations + prefix cache.

samir_p: can we propose a hybrid: baseline reserved capacity sized for steady 600 qps using quantized 13B/14B variant + a burst pool of compatible 70B instances (best-effort) that we only surface when cost/latency SLOs relax? that gives them predictability and an upgrade path.

jordan_pm: @samir_p sketch the numbers we need for intake: target p95 latency, SLO tiers (gold/silver), committed baseline qps, burst cap qps, acceptable fallback (e.g., degrade to 13B), and cost envelope. Also need EU region GPU type preference.

ryan_sales: customer says gold SLO p95 <=120ms for 95% of requests, silver <=250ms. Baseline = 600 qps committed, burst to 1800 qps for 10 mins / hour, monthly commit 24/7. Will accept fallback to 13B when p95 would exceed gold. EU region: frankfurt preferred.

mira_k: ok put that into an intake spec. I'll do a quick back-of-envelope sizing. assumptions: use 13B int8 (or q4) for baseline; 70B quantized for burst nodes; target GPU types: A100-80GB for baseline, H100 for burst if customer wants lowest latency.

mira_k: rough perf numbers (ballpark): 13B q4 on A100 -> ~70 tokens/s per GPU (with batching), 70B q4 on H100 -> ~120 tokens/s per GPU. For chat median output 80 tokens, so completions/s per GPU: 13B -> 0.875 req/s, 70B -> 1.5 req/s. To handle 600 qps steady on 13B we'd need ~700 GPUs? wait that's wrong, recalc: 600 req/s / 0.875 ~= 686 GPUs -> that's obviously unacceptable. Need to consider batching + dynamic batching gives higher effective throughput.

alex_f: Mira the tokens/s baseline numbers are conservative — continuous batching can increase throughput by 3-6x depending on latency tail. Also prefix KV caching for multi-turn chats will help a lot. We should do an expected efficiency multiplier.

samir_p: propose we run a micro-benchmark with representative convo set and measure effective req/s with our runtime (include batching & cache) — then produce a proposal: baseline reserved pool of N A100s running 13B quantized with autoscaling min size that handles 600 qps with p95 silver, and a burst pool of M H100s for gold SLO spikes.

mira_k: I'll flip numbers using a 4x batching efficiency assumption. Recalc: 13B effective req/s per A100 -> 0.875 *4 = 3.5 req/s -> need 600/3.5 ~= 172 GPUs. Still large. If we move baseline to multi-GPU model-parallel on H100s or use a 30B mid-tier it changes math.

ryan_sales: customer budget expects order-of-magnitude less than 172 GPUs. they'll push back. we need options: (A) smaller baseline using 30B quantized on fewer H100s with slightly worse quality, (B) hybrid with edge caching and client-side rate shaping, (C) suggest dedicated plus offload to hosted during bursts.

jordan_pm: decision matrix: quality vs cost vs latency. For intake deliverable let's prepare 3 SKU options with concrete numbers (GPUs, expected p95, cost range, operational constraints) + acceptance criteria and test plan. Assign owners: @mira_k run perf sims for SKU A/B/C, @alex_f evaluate kernel/runtime optimizations & feasible autoscale triggers, @samir_p draft playbook for fallback routing and rollout.

mira_k: will run sims. early timeline: 3 business days to get bench numbers using our workload harness in eu-west, will include k6 load script and sample convs.

alex_f: autoscale triggers we recommend: cpu/gpu utilization > 70% + token queue > X AND p95 latency > threshold. For burst pool use warm standby: keep 10% nodes warm and spin up remainder with preloaded model snapshot. spin-up target 90s for H100 pool.

samir_p: fallback routing plan: route to 13B variant when p95 gold likely violated, or fall back to hosted-graceful endpoint returning a short apology + degrade mode. We'll include canary + gradual traffic ramp in rollout criteria.

mira_k: sample k6 snippet I'll use for bench: ```
import http from 'k6/http'
import { sleep } from 'k6'
export default function(){
  let payload = JSON.stringify({model: 'redwood-13b-q4', input: '<<sample convo>>'})
  http.post('https://eu-api.redwood.ai/v1/generate', payload)
  sleep(0.1)
}
```

ryan_sales: perfect. next steps: Mira please upload results to the intake ticket and recommend the 3 SKU options. Jordan will mark this as P1 intake and prep scoping call with EdgeScale next Tue. I'll sync on pricing.

capacity-bot: Created ticket PROD-1248: "EdgeScale dedicated capacity intake" assigned to @jordan_pm. SLA: none set.

jordan_pm: thanks all. we'll capture launch criteria: 1) bench shows baseline meets silver SLO for 48h under synthetic + recorded traffic; 2) failover to 13B validated; 3) cost projection approved by finance; 4) infra runbook + rollback tested. aim to present options on Tue call. :calendar: :rocket:

ryan_sales: cc @EdgeScale contact on the call. I'll add them to the invite.

mira_k: uploading initial sim logs to ticket in ~72h.

alex_f: FYI we should also run a KV-cache effectiveness matrix — multi-turn savings could reduce GPU needs by 20-50%.

samir_p: noted. I'll add KV-cache tests to the bench plan.

ryan_sales: thanks team — going to prep the customer summary now. :thumbsup:
